```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(dsprrr)
old_cache <- configure_cache(enable = FALSE)
```

Most dsprrr optimizers keep a program's structure fixed and tune its
instructions or demonstrations. `flex()` *(experimental)* makes the program's
structure itself part of the search space: `GEPA()` can add or remove predictor
steps, introduce deterministic R logic, or call tools you expose.

| What should change? | Use | Execution boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Instructions or demos inside a fixed module | Regular `module()` + teleprompter | Standard host runtime |
| A bounded sequence of model steps | **JSON Flex** (`source_format = "json"`, default) | Validated data; no code interpreter |
| Branches, R logic, or host tools | **Executable Flex** (`source_format = "r"`) | Fresh runner; OS sandbox required by default |

Start with JSON Flex when the workflow is a pure graph of `Predict` and
`ChainOfThought` steps. Reach for executable R Flex only when deterministic
checks or tools can solve part of the task directly.

> **Note on the offline runner:** To execute end-to-end in documentation builds
> without API keys, this walkthrough uses a deterministic local Chat fixture
> (defined in a hidden setup chunk) and `r_code_runner()` over two reviewed
> source strings. A live search with `mcp_repl_runner()` and real ellmer Chats
> appears near the end of the page.

```{r}
#| label: offline-fixture
#| include: false
fixture_chat_class <- R6::R6Class(
  "Chat",
  public = list(
    turns = NULL,
    initialize = function(model, responder) {
      self$turns <- list()
      private$model <- ellmer::Model(name = model, extra_args = list())
      private$provider <- ellmer::Provider(name = "fixture", base_url = "")
      private$responder <- responder
    },
    chat = function(prompt, ...) {
      private$responder(paste(as.character(prompt), collapse = "\n"), NULL, ...)
    },
    chat_structured = function(prompt, type, ...) {
      private$responder(paste(as.character(prompt), collapse = "\n"), type, ...)
    },
    stream = function(...) character(),
    get_turns = function() self$turns,
    set_turns = function(turns) {
      self$turns <- turns
      invisible(self)
    },
    last_turn = function(role = NULL) NULL,
    get_model = function() private$model@name,
    get_provider = function() private$provider,
    get_model_object = function() private$model
  ),
  private = list(model = NULL, provider = NULL, responder = NULL),
  lock_objects = FALSE,
  parent_env = globalenv()
)

new_route_fixture <- function(
  proposed_source = NULL,
  model = "fixture-router"
) {
  audit <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
  audit$prompts <- character()
  audit$proposal_calls <- 0L
  audit$task_calls <- 0L

  responder <- function(prompt, type, ...) {
    prompt <- paste(as.character(prompt), collapse = "\n")
    audit$prompts <- c(audit$prompts, prompt)
    fields <- names(type@properties)

    if (identical(fields, "module_src")) {
      if (is.null(proposed_source)) {
        stop("The JSON example does not configure a proposer")
      }
      audit$proposal_calls <- audit$proposal_calls + 1L
      return(list(module_src = proposed_source))
    }

    if (!identical(fields, "queue")) {
      stop("Unexpected structured output requested by the fixture")
    }
    audit$task_calls <- audit$task_calls + 1L

    queue <- if (
      grepl("INC-DB-17|Queries time out|Read traffic", prompt, ignore.case = TRUE)
    ) {
      "database"
    } else if (
      grepl("INC-SEC-9|unusual-login|login spray", prompt, ignore.case = TRUE)
    ) {
      "security"
    } else if (
      grepl("INC-PAY-4|renewal|duplicate charge|Card charged twice", prompt, ignore.case = TRUE)
    ) {
      "payments"
    } else if (
      grepl("Password reset|Reset email", prompt, ignore.case = TRUE)
    ) {
      "identity"
    } else {
      stop("Unexpected ticket in the deterministic task fixture")
    }

    list(queue = queue)
  }

  list(
    chat = fixture_chat_class$new(model, responder),
    audit = audit
  )
}
```

## 1. Start with declarative JSON Flex

Calling `flex()` on a signature builds a one-step declarative JSON program by
default. JSON Flex checks field types ahead of time and needs no code
interpreter:

```{r}
#| label: json-example
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(dsprrr)

route_signature <- signature(
  "ticket -> queue: enum('database', 'security', 'payments', 'identity')",
  instructions = "Route each support ticket to its owning queue."
)

json_program <- flex(route_signature)
cat(json_program$module_src, "\n")
```

Run it like any other module:

```{r}
#| label: json-run
json_fixture <- new_route_fixture()

json_result <- run(
  json_program,
  ticket = "[INC-SEC-9] unusual-login burst",
  .llm = json_fixture$chat,
  .cache = FALSE,
  .return_format = "structured"
)

json_result$output
json_result$metadata$predictor_calls
```

## 2. Add a host tool with executable R Flex

Suppose a support team routes tickets to `database`, `security`, `payments`, or
`identity`. Some tickets carry an incident code whose owner already lives in an
internal catalog; the rest require an LLM call.

Keep `train` and `validation` separate during compilation, and hold out a third
dataset for the final check:

```{r}
#| label: router-data
train <- data.frame(
  ticket = c(
    "[INC-SEC-9] unusual-login burst",
    "Password reset links expire immediately"
  ),
  queue = c("security", "identity")
)

validation <- data.frame(
  ticket = c(
    "[INC-PAY-4] capture queue is growing",
    "Renewal created two invoices"
  ),
  queue = c("payments", "payments")
)
```

Expose the incident catalog as a plain host R function. Executable Flex calls
only the named tools you pass in—the optimizer never sees the closure's private
environment or the rest of your R session:

```{r}
#| label: router-tool
lookup_incident <- local({
  catalog <- c(
    "INC-DB-17" = "database",
    "INC-SEC-9" = "security",
    "INC-PAY-4" = "payments"
  )

  function(ticket) {
    hit <- names(catalog)[vapply(
      names(catalog),
      grepl,
      logical(1),
      x = ticket,
      fixed = TRUE
    )]
    if (!length(hit)) {
      return(list(found = FALSE))
    }
    list(found = TRUE, queue = unname(catalog[[hit[[1L]]]]))
  }
})

lookup_incident("[INC-DB-17] replicas unavailable")
lookup_incident("A password reset email is late")
```

An executable Flex program defines a top-level `forward()` function that can
call Flex primitives (`Predict()`, `ChainOfThought()`, `Prediction()`,
`ReAct()`, `RLM()`, `ProgramOfThought()`) alongside your named tools. Our
baseline calls a predictor on every ticket; the candidate we want GEPA to find
checks `lookup_incident()` first and falls back to the predictor only when the
catalog misses:

```{r}
#| label: router-sources
#| warning: false
baseline_source <- paste(
  "router <- Predict(\"$outer\", instructions = \"Choose the owning queue.\")",
  "forward <- function(ticket) router(ticket = ticket)",
  sep = "\n"
)

selected_fixture_source <- paste(
  "fallback <- Predict(\"$outer\", instructions = \"Route tickets without a known incident code.\")",
  "forward <- function(ticket) {",
  "  if (grepl(\"INC-\", ticket, fixed = TRUE)) {",
  "    hit <- lookup_incident(ticket = ticket)",
  "    if (isTRUE(hit$found)) return(Prediction(queue = hit$queue))",
  "  }",
  "  fallback(ticket = ticket)",
  "}",
  sep = "\n"
)

baseline <- flex(
  route_signature,
  module_src = baseline_source,
  tools = list(lookup_incident = lookup_incident),
  interpreter_factory = r_code_runner,
  source_format = "r",
  require_sandbox = FALSE,
  max_predictor_calls = 1L,
  max_tool_calls = 1L
)
```

Notice `require_sandbox = FALSE` with `r_code_runner()` (requires the optional
`callr` package). That is safe here *only* because both source strings are
reviewed fixtures; for live model-authored R code, keep the default
`require_sandbox = TRUE` with an OS-sandboxed runner such as
`mcp_repl_runner()`.

## 3. Reward efficiency with a trace-aware metric

A trace-aware metric (`metric_with_trace()`) can reward both accuracy and
avoiding unnecessary model calls: `1.0` for a right answer with zero predictor
calls, `0.5` for a right answer using a predictor, and `0.0` for a wrong route:

```{r}
#| label: router-metric
route_metric <- metric_with_trace(
  function(prediction, expected, program_trace) {
    correct <- identical(
      as.character(prediction$queue),
      as.character(expected$queue[[1L]])
    )
    predictor_calls <- program_trace$metadata$predictor_calls %||% 0L

    list(
      score = if (!correct) 0 else if (predictor_calls == 0L) 1 else 0.5,
      feedback = if (!correct) {
        sprintf("Expected '%s'; got '%s'.", expected$queue[[1L]], prediction$queue)
      } else if (predictor_calls > 0L) {
        "Correct route; prefer the incident catalog when it has an owner."
      } else {
        "Correct route without a predictor call."
      }
    )
  },
  field = "queue"
)
```

## 4. Compile with `GEPA()` and inspect the winning source

```{r}
#| label: router-compile
optimizer_fixture <- new_route_fixture(
  proposed_source = selected_fixture_source,
  model = "fixture-gepa-router"
)

optimized <- compile(
  baseline,
  GEPA(
    metric = route_metric,
    population_size = 2L,
    generations = 1L,
    selection = "current_best",
    track_best_outputs = TRUE,
    verbose = FALSE
  ),
  trainset = train,
  valset = validation,
  .llm = optimizer_fixture$chat,
  control = optimizer_control(
    max_metric_calls = 40L,
    max_provider_calls = 30L,
    max_elapsed_seconds = 300,
    num_threads = 1L,
    progress = FALSE
  )
)

compile_result <- optimization_result(optimized)
compile_result
```

The source GEPA selected is stored directly on the compiled module—always
inspect it before deploying:

```{r}
#| label: router-source-review
cat(optimized$module_src, "\n")
```

## 5. Compare once on untouched holdout tickets

Evaluate both the baseline and compiled programs on six fresh tickets (three
with catalog incident codes, three without):

```{r}
#| label: router-holdout
holdout <- data.frame(
  ticket = c(
    "[INC-DB-17] replicas unavailable",
    "[INC-SEC-9] login spray detected",
    "[INC-PAY-4] payment capture is delayed",
    "Reset email arrives after its token expires",
    "Duplicate charge after a plan upgrade",
    "Read traffic fails after failover"
  ),
  queue = c("database", "security", "payments", "identity", "payments", "database")
)

accuracy <- metric_exact_match(field = "queue")
before_fixture <- new_route_fixture(model = "fixture-holdout-before")
after_fixture <- new_route_fixture(model = "fixture-holdout-after")

before <- evaluate(
  baseline, holdout, metric = accuracy,
  .llm = before_fixture$chat, .cache = FALSE, .progress = FALSE
)
after <- evaluate(
  optimized, holdout, metric = accuracy,
  .llm = after_fixture$chat, .cache = FALSE, .progress = FALSE
)

count_calls <- function(res, field) {
  sum(vapply(res$metadata, function(m) as.integer(m[[field]] %||% 0L), integer(1)))
}

heldout <- data.frame(
  program = c("baseline", "selected"),
  exact_match = c(before$mean_score, after$mean_score),
  predictor_calls = c(
    count_calls(before, "predictor_calls"),
    count_calls(after, "predictor_calls")
  ),
  tool_calls = c(
    count_calls(before, "tool_calls"),
    count_calls(after, "tool_calls")
  )
)
heldout
```

Both programs route all six holdout tickets accurately (`1.0`), while the
selected Flex program cuts predictor calls in half (6 → 3) by resolving catalog
incidents locally through `lookup_incident()`.

```{r}
#| label: verify-invariants
#| include: false
gepa_budget <- compile_result$budget
compile_prompts <- paste(optimizer_fixture$audit$prompts, collapse = "\n")
stopifnot(
  identical(json_result$output, list(queue = "security")),
  identical(json_result$metadata$predictor_calls, 1L),
  length(intersect(train$ticket, validation$ticket)) == 0L,
  length(intersect(holdout$ticket, c(train$ticket, validation$ticket))) == 0L,
  !any(vapply(holdout$ticket, grepl, logical(1), x = compile_prompts, fixed = TRUE)),
  identical(compile_result$status, "completed"),
  isTRUE(gepa_budget$metric_calls <= gepa_budget$limits$max_metric_calls),
  isTRUE(gepa_budget$provider_calls <= gepa_budget$limits$max_provider_calls),
  identical(gepa_budget$provider_calls, optimizer_fixture$audit$task_calls + optimizer_fixture$audit$proposal_calls),
  isTRUE(all.equal(compile_result$best_score, 0.75)),
  identical(optimized$module_src, selected_fixture_source),
  isTRUE(before$mean_score == 1 && after$mean_score == 1),
  identical(heldout$predictor_calls, c(6L, 3L)),
  identical(heldout$tool_calls, c(0L, 3L))
)
```

## 6. Run a live sandboxed search

For live model-authored R code, install `mcptools` and Posit's `mcp-repl`
sandbox ([posit-dev/mcp-console](https://github.com/posit-dev/mcp-console)) and
keep `require_sandbox = TRUE` (the default):

```sh
Rscript -e 'install.packages("mcptools")'
uv tool install posit-mcp-repl
```

```{r}
#| label: live-gepa
#| eval: false
live_baseline <- flex(
  route_signature,
  module_src = baseline_source,
  tools = list(lookup_incident = lookup_incident),
  interpreter_factory = function() mcp_repl_runner(timeout = 45),
  source_format = "r",
  max_predictor_calls = 1L,
  max_tool_calls = 1L
)

live_optimized <- compile(
  live_baseline,
  GEPA(
    metric = route_metric,
    population_size = 4L,
    generations = 2L,
    selection = "current_best",
    seed = 42L,
    verbose = FALSE
  ),
  trainset = train,
  valset = validation,
  .llm = ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-6-luna"),
  .reflection_llm = ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-6-astra"),
  control = optimizer_control(
    max_metric_calls = 80L,
    max_provider_calls = 50L,
    max_cost = 1,
    progress = FALSE
  )
)

optimization_result(live_optimized)
```

## Operational limits to keep in mind

- `max_predictor_calls` and `max_tool_calls` bound direct calls per invocation
  (nested `ReAct()` / `RLM()` predictors have their own step bounds).
- Guest R code replays from the top after each bridged predictor or tool call,
  so keep guest-side logic pure and bound loops explicitly.
- Host tools run in your R session with their own permissions, even when guest
  source runs inside `mcp_repl_runner()`.
- Executable Flex evaluates dataset rows sequentially and does not stream
  tokens.

When the workflow structure is already known, a plain `module()` or `pipeline()`
is simpler and cheaper; see [Choose an optimizer](advanced-optimization.html)
for the other optimization strategies.

```{r}
#| label: restore-cache
#| include: false
if (is.null(old_cache)) {
  configure_cache(enable = TRUE)
} else {
  do.call(configure_cache, old_cache)
}
```
